title: Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!
subtitle: Kanto with a partner at the player’s side
summary: Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee! are Game Freak's Switch reimaginings of Pokémon Yellow, released on 16 November 2018.
body: Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee! are Game Freak's Switch reimaginings of Pokémon Yellow, released on 16 November 2018. The player returns to Kanto with Pikachu or Eevee as a close companion, collecting Pokémon and challenging Trainers and Gym Leaders. The familiar landscape is presented around creatures visibly moving in the environment. Choosing which one to approach becomes part of exploration, while the partner traveling beside the player gives the two versions a personal relationship at the center of the larger collection.

Wild encounters use a catching system influenced by Pokémon Go. Berries and timed Poké Ball throws replace the usual battle against an ordinary wild Pokémon, while Trainer battles retain the party's turn-based attacks. Joy-Con gestures or the optional Poké Ball Plus connect the throw to a physical action. A second person can join with another controller and assist in encounters and battles. The design creates different kinds of cooperation: the Pokémon party works within the battle, and another player can help guide the journey from outside it.

Pikachu or Eevee can be dressed up and signals nearby hidden items, while other Pokémon can follow or carry the player through Kanto. Connectivity with Pokémon Go brings another route into the collection. Junichi Masuda directed the games, and Shota Kageyama arranged their music. The release sought both returning players and newcomers, joining a recognizable early adventure to the catching gestures many had learned on a phone. It made Kanto another meeting point between the series' long console history and its much wider mobile audience.
